# AGENTS.md

How agents work in this repository. The rules are in [ai/RULES.md](ai/RULES.md) and win over
anything here; this file is the operational summary.

## What this is

droid-observatory: a Tauri 2 + Leptos (Rust) desktop app that shows a Factory Mission moving
through nine lanes, with validation, gate, agent attribution, waste and cost per sub-droid.
PRD: `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md`. Spec: `SPEC.md` (approved 2026-10-22; the mission plans from it).

Current state: no application code. The walking skeleton (core crate, canonical `Event`,
`observatory replay` over one captured session, an empty board that starts) is the first
thing the mission lands, before any milestone deepens its area.

## Setup, build, test

```sh
make doctor          # tool check with install hints
make hooks           # enable .githooks (once)
make check           # all light checks = mission-branch CI
make fmt             # rustfmt (no-op until Cargo.toml exists)
make lint            # clippy -D warnings
make test            # cargo test --workspace
make deny            # cargo-deny advisories, licences, bans
make replay-fixtures # observatory-cli replay over fixtures/streams/*.jsonl
make app-dev         # Tauri dev window (after the app exists)
```

Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` (1.99.1, rustfmt, clippy, wasm32 target). Do not change it
without a decision file.

## Runtime limits (measured)

Measured 2026-10-22 on the owner's machine; source `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-validation-readiness.md`
(SPEC §5.8):

- At most 3 concurrent agent-browser validator sessions per `trunk serve` (1.34-1.54 GB RSS each,
  CPU negligible idle); use `--session <name>` per validator.
- `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (1-min load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10 cores during the scratch run).
- All cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock
  (`Blocking waiting for file lock on build directory`); expect waits, not failures.
- `trunk serve` and `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns port 3141
  (`cargo tauri dev` starts its own); killing `cargo-tauri` alone orphans trunk and the app binary.
- Cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s, incremental 1.46-2.08 s, `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
- The Tauri window has no CDP endpoint; validators use the smoke check (process alive, `Running`
  log line, WebKit connections on 3141, System Events listing) plus the browser path on 3141.

## Interactive QA path

Until the app exists: `make check` is the only runnable target.
Once the skeleton lands, the path the validators follow is:

1. `make doctor` reports no missing required tools.
2. `cargo run -p observatory-cli -- replay fixtures/streams/<capture>.jsonl` prints lane
   events and ends with `unknown events: 0`.
3. `make app-dev` opens the window; open the same fixture (Replay); the nine lanes render
   and a card opens its Details view.
4. With the window open, start `droid exec --mission ...` in a terminal; the new session
   appears on the board (Attach) and each event shows within 1 s.

No login gate: the app watches and reads local session files and uses the GitHub token from the keychain or
`GITHUB_TOKEN` only for the gate lane.

## Layout and ownership

```text
crates/observatory-core   ingest, model, metrics, store, control (no UI deps)
crates/observatory-cli    headless replay/inspect over core
apps/observatory-app      Tauri 2 shell + Leptos UI
fixtures/streams          captured mission streams, named <YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl
docs/decisions            D-NNN-slug.md, one per decision; README.md is generated
docs/runbooks             recovery procedures: red gate, fix cycle, stall, hooks, release
reports/                  usage, waste, readiness; pasted from tools
build-log/                tool-call log written by .factory hooks
ai/                       PRD, rules, template, session logs
```

Crate and app paths are the contract the Makefile and CI probe for; keep them.

## Conventions

- Rust 2024 edition, `rustfmt.toml` and `clippy.toml` as committed. Warnings are errors.
- Naming: standard Rust (`snake_case` items and modules, `CamelCase` types, `SCREAMING_SNAKE`
  consts). Event kinds mirror the PRD §7 names in `snake_case`
  (`finding.blocking` → `FindingBlocking`). Lane and role enums use the PRD's words.
- Tests: unit tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` next to the code; integration tests in
  `crates/<crate>/tests/<topic>.rs`; fixture-driven tests read `fixtures/streams/`. Test
  functions read as sentences: `rework_window_closes_on_resolution()`.
- Tests before code (rule 1): commit the red test, then the code that turns it green.
- No magic numbers: every threshold lives in `config/observatory.example.toml` with a reason.
- Debt markers: `TODO(#123)` or `TODO(B-123)`; anything else fails `make check-todos`.
- Markdown: `.markdownlint-cli2.yaml`; links must resolve (`make check-links`).
- Files over 200 KB fail CI unless under `fixtures/streams/` or `build-log/`.

## Git

- Forward only (rule 12): never amend, reset, rebase, stash, or force-push. Fix with a new
  commit. `.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` and `.githooks/pre-push` enforce this.
- Nothing reaches `main` except the mission's single pull request. `main` has a ruleset:
  PR required, `gate` check required, no force push, no bypass.
- Milestones live in worktrees and integrate into `mission/<name>`. Two worktrees never edit
  the same file (rule 13); shared files (`SPEC.md` §9–10, `README.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
  `docs/decisions/README.md`) are written by the orchestrator at integration time.
- Commit subject under 72 characters; co-author trailer for agent commits:
  `Co-authored-by: factory-droid[bot] <138933559+factory-droid[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>`.

## Decisions, backlog, logs

- A decision is one file: `docs/decisions/D-NNN-slug.md` with `**Date:**`, `**Status:**`,
  context, decision, alternatives, consequences. Run `make decisions-index` after adding one.
- Deferred work goes to the backlog (GitHub issues labelled `backlog`, indexed in `BACKLOG.md`)
  as `B-NNN` with a reason, not into TODOs (rule 14).
- Every session is logged under `ai/session/` with transcript links; every tool call is
  logged to `build-log/` by the PostToolUse hook. Do not disable the hooks.
- Usage and waste per milestone go to `reports/` pasted from the tool that produced them.

## Mission setup

Models per role (rule 19; `.factory/settings.json`; D-006):

| Role | Model |
|---|---|
| Orchestrator | `claude-fable-5.1` |
| Workers | `claude-sonnet-5-5` |
| Validators (scrutiny, user testing) | `claude-opus-5-5` |

Command: see README "Running it as a mission".
Reasoning effort: orchestrator `high`, workers `high`, validators `high` (SPEC §2).
A model change is a decision file.

The human answers only at milestone boundaries or when the stall flag is up (rule 15).
Deviations from the spec are proposed with reason and cost, and wait for approval (rule 9).

## Environment and secrets

See `.env.example`. Secrets come from the OS keychain (`droid-observatory/<name>` entries)
or the environment, never from the repository, the store, or logs. Raw session JSONL may
contain secrets: render read-only, never upload, never copy into the store.

- The GitHub token is a read-only fine-grained PAT; read check results via Actions runs
  (`/repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs`) and commit statuses (`/repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), not the
  Checks API (no Checks permission). Keychain items are generic passwords with service
  `droid-observatory/<name>` (see `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md`).

Grafana Cloud OTLP (`OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*`) is the telemetry backend; export is off unless
`[telemetry].enabled = true`.

## Do not

- Add a dependency without `make deny` passing and a version verified on the day (rule 3).
- Write to `main`, rewrite history, or touch another worktree's files.
- Estimate a count, timing or token number: paste it from the tool (rule 7).
- Drop an unknown event: count it and show it (rule 18).
</coding_guidelines>

# Planning notes for mission artifacts (orchestrator, 2026-10-22)

Read this before any other mission file. It records what the owner decided after `SPEC.md` v0.2 was
written, and the readiness facts the mission is built on. Where these notes and `SPEC.md` disagree,
these notes win (owner decisions after the spec); `SPEC.md` is amended as-built at the next
integration (RULES rule 8). Where these notes are silent, `SPEC.md` is the authority.

Repository: `/home/user/code/EllyaOrg/projects/dalimaray/droid-observatory` (GitHub `dctellya/droid-observatory`).
Mission branch: `mission/observatory-v1` (created from `main` at `c8524c2`; pre-mission commit `2266d3e`).
Owner: David Carbajosa Tesoro (`dct`, GitHub `dctellya`).

## Files to read for context (all in the repository)

- `SPEC.md` (v0.2): §2 mission setup, §3 milestones S, M0–M5 with named tests and acceptance
  commands, §4 versions, §5 architecture, §6 tests, §7 CI, §8 deliverables.
- `ai/RULES.md` (binding), `AGENTS.md` (operational summary), `ai/prd/droid-observatory-prd.md` v0.6

- `reports/readiness/2026-10-22-dependency-readiness.md` and

- `config/observatory.example.toml`, `deny.toml`, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/*.yml`,

## Owner decisions after SPEC v0.1 (2026-10-22), all binding

1. **Session file schema.** Droid session files carry no Droid version. The mapping version is
   selected from the Droid version recorded in the **fixture header** (`droid --version`, 0.247.0
   at capture). Token usage, model, tags and child linkage are read from the sibling
   `<session-id>.settings.json` (`tokenUsage`, `childInclusiveTokenUsageBySessionId`,
   `inclusiveTokenUsage`, `lastCallTokenUsage`, `assistantActiveTimeMs`, `tags`, `model`,
   `reasoningEffort`, `interactionMode`, `autonomyLevel`). Child sessions are sibling files linked by
   `session_start.callingSessionId` / `callingToolUseId`. JSONL `type` values seen: `message`,
   `todo_state`, `agent_turn_outcome`, `compaction_state`, `session_start`; `modelId`,
   `apiProvider`, `reasoningEffort` sit on assistant messages. Decision file at S integration; SPEC
   §3 M0 / §5.2 amended as-built then.
2. **Keyring.** `keyring-core` 1.0.1 + `apple-native-keyring-store` 1.0.2 (feature `keychain`,
   `set_default_store`) instead of `keyring` 4.x (fails `cargo deny`). Keychain items are generic
   passwords with service `droid-observatory/<name>` and account = the login user (`dct`), not the
   item name. Items present: `droid-observatory/github-token`, `droid-observatory/otlp-headers`.
   Decision file at S integration.
3. **DMG** only in the CI `bundle` job; local builds produce `.app` (`bundle.targets: ["app"]`).
4. **Tauri evidence.** Validators treat the Tauri window as a smoke check (process alive, `Running`
   log line, WebKit connections to port 3141, System Events lists the app). The browser surface
   (`trunk serve --port 3141` driven by `agent-browser`) is the primary interactive surface. At each
   milestone integration the owner takes one real screenshot with the display unlocked, attached to
   the report.
5. **Concurrency limits** (now SPEC §5.8 v0.2): max 3 concurrent agent-browser sessions per
   `trunk serve` (1.34–1.54 GB RSS each); `cargo llvm-cov` runs alone (load 3.3 → 14.6 on 10
   cores); all cargo builds serialize on the shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` lock; `trunk serve` and
   `cargo tauri dev` coexist only when exactly one trunk owns 3141; cold `trunk serve` 55.94 s,
   incremental 1.46–2.08 s; `cargo tauri dev` to running app 37.66 s.
6. **GitHub token** is a fine-grained **read-only** PAT (Contents, Issues, Pull requests, Actions,
   Commit statuses, Metadata; repos droid-observatory and artstudio). No Checks permission: read
   check results through Actions runs (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/actions/runs?head_sha=`) and commit
   statuses (`GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{sha}/status`), never the check-runs API.
7. **M4 exit (supersedes SPEC §3 M4 acceptance "merge from the app").** Merge button is visible when
   the policy allows and checks are green; with the read-only token the app surfaces the 403 cleanly
   (clear message naming the PR, target and missing permission; no crash, no retry storm); the
   **owner** performs the merge (UI or API); the badge updates from the poll (`policy-merged` or
   `merged` as detected). The write-token question stays at the M3→M4 boundary.
8. **Throttling and caps.** At a Factory usage throttle (5-hour / 7-day / monthly limits) or at a
   milestone cap, the run pauses at the point reached, usage so far is written to
   `reports/usage/`, the stall flag goes up and the owner is asked. **No silent model or
   reasoning-effort downgrade, ever** (a change is a decision file, rule 19). The M0-boundary re-cap
   of M1–M5 from measured S and M0 usage stays.
9. **Backlog = `BACKLOG.md` only.** No GitHub issues, no `scripts/gen-backlog.sh`, no `backlog`
   label. SPEC §8 "hybrid backlog" item is withdrawn; decision file at S integration records this.
   `AGENTS.md` and RULES rule 14 wording to be aligned (rule 14 is the owner's file; proposed

## 1. System overview and invariants

A Factory Mission writes one JSONL per agent session under `~/.factory/sessions/<cwd-slug>/`.
`observatory-core` turns those lines (and, later, a hosted JSON-RPC stream, local git and GitHub)
into canonical `Event`s on nine lanes, indexes them in SQLite by pointer, computes views and
metrics; `observatory-cli` exercises core headlessly; `observatory-app` (Tauri 2 shell + Leptos
CSR UI) renders the board. Attach (watch + tail) is the primary live mode; replay is attach at
end of file; host is the secondary path and the only one with a control channel (D-008).

Invariants every worker must keep (a violation is a blocking finding):

| # | Invariant | Where enforced |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | `observatory-core` is synchronous: no `tokio`, no `async fn` in its public API. tokio lives only in `apps/observatory-app/src-tauri`. | `cargo machete` + review; `Cargo.toml` of core has no async runtime |
| I2 | The UI holds no logic: card position, filters, scrubbing, tray count, details data, library entries are functions in `core::view`, unit-tested there. The Leptos crate only renders what the shell sends. | SPEC §6 "UI logic" |
| I3 | Raw lines are read-only and never copied into the store. The store keeps `path, byte_offset, byte_len`; the line is re-read on demand. `~/.factory/sessions/` is never written. | `store` DDL has no payload column; `JsonlSource` opens files read-only |
| I4 | Every `Event` carries `mapping_version` and a `SourcePtr`. | type system; test `every_event_carries_the_mapping_version()` |
| I5 | Unknown raw lines become `EventKind::Unknown { raw_type }`, are counted and shown (tray, CLI final line `unknown events: N`, exported counter), never dropped. | `mapping::map_record` is total: it always returns at least one `Event` |

### 4.1 Source trait and RawRecord

```rust
pub struct RawRecord { pub ptr: SourcePtr, pub session_id: SessionId, pub bytes: Vec<u8> /* one line, no newline */ }
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)] #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]

pub trait Source {
    fn kind(&self) -> SourceKind;
    /// Pull the next records. Returns an empty Vec when nothing new is available right now.

}
```

## 9. Metrics (`core::metrics`, M5)

Time states (PRD §10.1): `enum TimeState { Active, WaitingHuman(Question|Permission|Merge), WaitingValidation,
RetryFailure, IdleQueued, IdleUnscheduled }`. `pub fn partition(events_of_feature: &[Event], end: Timestamp)
-> Vec<Interval { from, to, state }>`, contiguous and non-overlapping
(`time_states_partition_every_instant_exactly_once()`). Active intervals `[arch decision]`: each event
with `duration` contributes `[at, at + duration]`; `duration` is set by the mapper as `tool_result.at -
tool_use.at` for tool calls and `assistant.at - previous_line.at` (same session) for model generation.
`ToolError`/`HookBlocked` intervals are `RetryFailure`; an open `QuestionAsked`/`PermissionRequested`/
green-but-unmerged gate with no active interval is `WaitingHuman`; `TaskDone` without a validator start is
`WaitingValidation`; a defined feature blocked by another's active interval is `IdleQueued`, else
`IdleUnscheduled`. The oracle (below) validates these rules.

Rework windows (`metrics::rework`): open/close pairs from PRD §10.2 (`FindingBlocking→ReworkResolved`,
`QaScenarioFailed→QaScenarioPassed` same scenario, `IntegrationConflict→IntegrationConflictResolved`,
`CheckFailed→CheckPassed` same check); overlapping windows on one feature merge; unresolved at mission end
reported with `closed_by = None`. Causes: `scrutiny`, `user_testing`, `integration`, `gate`.
Overhead (`metrics::overhead`): orchestrator intervals before the first `FeatureDefined`, replanning not
attributable, and compaction recovery; reported as its own line; `[metrics].overhead_apportionment =
"equal"` splits it and labels the output `apportioned`. Derived (`metrics::derived`): cycle (feature,
milestone, mission, per lane), waste by the 8 SPEC §5.6 causes, bottleneck (lane/role with highest
waiting + queued; lane with highest WIP/throughput), fix loops (count of `fix` cycles).

Cost (`metrics::cost`): tokens from `UsageReported` (sidecar `tokenUsage`); credits primary when
`factoryCredits` is present; otherwise `Σ tokens × per_m / 1e6` from `config/prices/<date>.toml`
(`[metrics].price_table`); every `Cost` carries `price_table: String` (the `effective` date)
(`cost_names_the_price_table_date()`). Budget meter: `[metrics].budget` or the launch `budget_usd`.

`first_pass_active_s_per_completed_feature`.

## 3. Milestones

Seven milestones on the board of the build: the walking skeleton `S` first (rule 2), then
`M0`–`M5` in PRD §13 order. PRD §13 counts six; the seventh is the skeleton rule 2 requires, so
the PRD count is superseded here (rule 8). A milestone is integrated into the mission branch, never
shipped. The spec itself is not a milestone: it is approved before the mission starts.

**B-010 settled: skeleton before M0, and the capture is this mission.** Rule 2 wants the thinnest
end-to-end slice first; PRD §13 wants M0 to freeze the mapping before M1–M5 are planned in detail.
Both hold because the capture needs no extra mission: the moment the owner runs the §2 command, the
orchestrator's session JSONL is growing under `~/.factory/sessions/`, and the skeleton's workers
and validators add child sessions for every role. `S` replays a snapshot of that file through a
mapper that knows nothing yet (every line is `unknown.event`, counted). `M0` snapshots the same
sessions again at `S` integration, now with all four roles present, freezes it as the fixture,
and drives the unknown count to zero. The optional B-009 pre-capture is not needed; a small
sample-repo mission (PRD §13 M0) is the fallback only if role identification cannot be established
from this mission's own files.

**Common to every milestone.**

- Tests first (rule 1): each feature begins with a red test committed in the worktree; the
  scrutiny validator checks that the red run exists in the worker's log.
- Acceptance commands are the ones in §6 and `make check`; counts are pasted, not estimated.
- Exit needs: `make check` green on the mission branch after integration, `mission-checks` green
  on the push, zero blocking findings open, §9/§10 rows written, README/BACKLOG/decisions index
  updated (rule 16), `reports/usage/<m>.md` and `reports/readiness/<date>-<m>.json` added
  (B-015), and no `unknown.event` on the capture if the milestone adds a source (rule 18).
- Must not touch: `main`, another milestone's worktree, `rust-toolchain.toml` without a decision,
  the shared files (§2), the ruleset on `main`.
- Fixtures: `fixtures/streams/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.jsonl` is the orchestrator session; its child
  sessions live in `fixtures/streams/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.children/<session-id>.jsonl` with the
  `.settings.json` beside each. A fixture is committed only after `gitleaks detect --no-git` on the
  directory is clean and a reviewer has read it; raw lines may carry tool output.

# D-007: Ruleset on main

**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Status:** accepted

## Context

`main` is the gate the observatory watches. Its rules must be the ones the PRD's merge
policy reader (FR-G4) will find, and they must not hang the final PR.

## Decision

GitHub ruleset `main-gate`, enforcement active, target `refs/heads/main`:

- pull request required, **required approving reviews: 0** (the human merges by hand; the
  gate is the review), dismiss stale reviews on push, conversation resolution not required,
  `require_extra_approval_for_unattributed_changes` off (the API default of on was found
  after the first merge and switched off by the owner on 2026-10-22);
- required status check: **`gate`** (from `gate.yml`), strict (branch up to date);
- deletion blocked, non-fast-forward (force push) blocked;
- no bypass actors: admins included.

## Alternatives

Legacy branch protection (superseded by rulesets); admin bypass for the first PR (would
let the readiness PR skip the gate it introduces); requiring every job by name (D-003).

## Consequences

Applied with `gh api` on 2026-10-22 and recorded in `ai/session/`. Direct pushes to `main`
fail for everyone, including the owner; `.githooks/pre-push` and
`.factory/hooks/guard-git.sh` refuse them earlier.

  pull_request:
    branches:

  workflow_call:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    outputs:

    steps:

      - name: actionlint

## PRD @95
## 8. Board model

**Card = one milestone.** The milestone is the spec phase: the orchestrator plans it, workers build its features in a worktree, validators judge it, and it integrates into `mission/<name>`. Each card lists its features with their individual state, and metrics roll up feature → milestone → mission.

A card moves left to right. Its position is the lane where its most recent open activity is. The Details view shows the full history across lanes.

**Gate group.** Lane 8 holds one group per mission: the mission PR. All cards of the mission share that gate state; the badge sits on the group. Until the PR exists, lane 8 shows the mission branch with its fast-check status as a pre-gate placeholder.

**Fix loop.** When CI goes red on the mission PR, the observatory reopens the mission on `mission/<name>` with a cycle tagged `fix` on the milestone(s) whose features the fix touches. Those cards are drawn with a loop arrow back into lane 3. The PR stays the same. The loop is counted as rework in lane 9.

**Mission completion.** Mission state is `complete` only when the PR is merged with CI green. Until then it is `planning`, `building`, `validating`, `at gate`, or `fixing`.

### 8.1 Card anatomy

```text
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ M2  Host                                    [Details]│
│ features 4/6 done · worktree wt/m2 · mission/obs-v1  │
│ ● validation: RED (1 blocking)  ◆ branch: fast checks ✓│
│ now: worker-3 (claude-sonnet-5-5) on F-014 · 00:14:22 │
│ cycle 2h 10m · waste 38m (rework 22m, human 16m)      │
│ 412k tok · $1.84 (prices 2026-10-22)                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Gate group (lane 8):
┌── PR #41  mission/observatory-v1 → main ─────────────┐
│ ◆ gate: HUMAN REQUIRED · checks 7/7 ✓ · attested ✓     │
│ cards: M0 M1 M2 M3 M4 M5                      [Merge]  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Validation badge** (card): GREEN when scrutiny passed and user-testing scenarios passed for all features on the latest build; RED when any blocking finding or failed scenario is open; GREY when not yet validated.
- **Branch badge** (card): fast checks on `mission/<name>` passed / failed / running for this milestone's integration.
- **Gate badge** (group): `pending` (no PR), `checks running`, `review requested`, `human required`, `ruleset blocked`, `policy-merged`, `CI green`, `CI red`.
- **Now**: the agent currently holding a feature of this card (role, model, session id, feature, time on task). Empty when idle, with the idle reason (waiting on human, waiting on validation, queued).
- **Merge** button (group): only visible when the gate policy requires a human merge and checks are green.

## PRD @327
### 11.3 Security

- GitHub token and Factory credentials stay in the OS keychain (Tauri keyring plugin). Never written to the store or logs.
- Raw JSONL may contain secrets from tool output; the app renders it read-only and never uploads it.
- Merge is the only outward-facing write. It requires an explicit confirmation naming the PR and target branch.

## PRD @196
### 9.7 Mission lifecycle (FR-L)

- FR-L1: Attach (primary live mode): watch `~/.factory/sessions/` with a filesystem notifier, detect any new session JSONL (a mission started from any terminal on this machine), tail it as it grows and render it within 1 s, named by its `--tag` or session id. No control channel.
- FR-L2: Replay a finished mission from JSONL files. Same adapter as attach: replay is attach at end-of-file, with the scrubber.
- FR-L3: Host (secondary path): launch a mission from the app: choose repo, mission file, mission branch name, models and reasoning effort for orchestrator / worker / validator, autonomy flags, optional budget. The app spawns `droid exec --mission --input-format stream-jsonrpc --output-format stream-jsonrpc`; this is the only mode with a control channel (pause, message, answer).
- FR-L4: Mission library: list past missions with headline metrics.
